newsitem.title: UK: UK business divided on merits of single mkt-IoD.
newsitem.headline: UK business divided on merits of single mkt-IoD.

text.p: British businesses appear to be divided over the merits of the single European market, a survey by the Institute of Directors showed on Monday.
More than half of the 500 company directors quizzed, 54 percent, said they had benefited from the opening of trade, with one in four seeing profitability and export levels rise.

However 38 percent of those surveyed said the cost of doing business in Europe had increased, largely due to the bureaucracy firms come up against in the form of single market and European Union regulations, the IoD said.
More than three quarters of the survey said they had been affected in some way by the introduction of the single European market.

Despite the bringing down of barriers, some obstacles still existed to hinder UK companies, such as the continuing provision of aid by some member states, ineffective competition policy, the uneven application of technical standards and over-complicated rules, the survey said.
Large to medium-sized companies firms had a more favourable experience than smaller firms, the survey found, with the manufacturing sector benefiting more than service-orientated companies.
IoD business economist Alison Cansfield said the institute was strongly supportive of the single market and was convinced it helped many UK firms to secure a competitive edge.
"But more attention needs to be focused on cutting the costs of complying with single market legislation and clamping down on barriers to trade," she said.
